<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S5.SS3" title="In 5 Findings ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">5.3 </span>Dimension neglect: models under-detect geometry-driven constraints</span></a></li>
</ol></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_section"><a href="#S6" title="In CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">6 </span>Conclusion</span></a></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_bibliography"><a href="#bib" title="In CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title">References</span></a></li>
</ol></nav>

</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have shown remarkable progress in Vision-Language Navigation (VLN), offering new possibilities for navigation decision-making that could benefit both robotic platforms and human users. However, real-world navigation is inherently conditioned by the agent’s mobility constraints. For example, a sweeping robot cannot traverse stairs, while a quadruped can. We introduce Capability-Conditioned Navigation (<span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">CapNav</span>), a benchmark designed to evaluate how well VLMs can navigate complex indoor spaces given an agent’s specific physical and operational capabilities. CapNav defines five representative human and robot agents, each described with physical dimensions, mobility capabilities, and environmental interaction abilities. CapNav provides 45 real-world indoor scenes, 473 navigation tasks, and 2365 QA pairs to test if VLMs can traverse indoor environments based on agent capabilities. We evaluate 13 modern VLMs and find that current VLM’s navigation performance drops sharply as mobility constraints tighten, and that even state-of-the-art models struggle with obstacle types that require reasoning on spatial dimensions. We conclude by discussing the implications for capability-aware navigation and the opportunities for advancing embodied spatial reasoning in future VLMs. The benchmark is available at <a href="https://github.com/makeabilitylab/CapNav" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">https://github.com/makeabilitylab/CapNav</a></p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<div id="p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="p1.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></p>
</div>
<div id="id9" class="ltx_logical-block">
    
<div id="p2" class="ltx_para"><img src="2602.18424v1/io.png" id="g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:685/217;" width="685" height="217" alt="[Uncaptioned image]">
</div>
    
<figure id="S0.F1" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S0.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S0.F1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">We introduce Capability-Conditioned Navigation (<span id="S0.F1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">CapNav</span>), a benchmark designed to evaluate how well VLMs can navigate complex indoor spaces given an agent’s specific physical and operational capabilities. CapNav inputs (1) a tour video of an indoor space, (2) nodes of its navigation graph, (3) an agent’s mobility profile, and (4) a navigation task, and evaluates VLM outputs in task feasibility, path validity, route traversability, and reasoning validity.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<figure id="S1.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18424v1/example_case.png" id="S1.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:617/219;" width="617" height="219" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S1.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The CapNav benchmark evaluates whether VLMs can correctly ground differences in agent mobility capabilities when generating navigation plans. This example demonstrates a navigation task that has different feasibility and path for different agents.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As vision–language models (VLMs) advance in visual grounding <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>]</cite> and spatial reasoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>, they are now commonly used as drop-in “navigation assistants” or planning modules for robots and assistive systems <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>, <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">66</a>, <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite>. Guiding people to reach destinations <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>, <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite> and controlling robots in movement decisions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite>, they are widely applied in open-ended scenarios where solutions can be pluralistic, and their plausibility depends on the agents’ movement capabilities.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Consider the multi‑story building shown in <a href="#S1.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 2</span></a>. To go from the basement foyer to the top-floor rest area, a wheelchair user should use the elevator, but a quadruped robot can only go up the stairwell (since it cannot operate the elevator). Similarly, a non-disabled human may squeeze through a cluttered corridor, while a wide humanoid robot cannot. Without awareness of capability, VLM may recommend routes that are infeasible or even unsafe for a given agent  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Such mobility constraints and the pluralistic nature of navigation remain underexplored in prior vision–language navigation research. Existing frameworks and benchmarks evaluate embodiment-agnostic goal-reaching in simulated or graph-based environments <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>, <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>, <a href="#bib.bib62" title="" class="ltx_ref">54</a>, <a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite>, or reduce navigation to simplified VQA-style spatial reasoning tasks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>, <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">57</a>, <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">63</a>, <a href="#bib.bib63" title="" class="ltx_ref">61</a>]</cite>. Moreover, evaluation protocols typically measure trajectory fidelity against a single annotated ground-truth path <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite>. Consequently, these paradigms overlook the capability-conditioned validity and solution multiplicity that characterize real-world navigation — limitations that become increasingly critical as VLMs are deployed in embodied control and assistive scenarios.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">CapNav</span>, a benchmark for VLM’s navigation validity across varying mobility constraints. We consider five representative embodiments: adults with no motor disabilities, wheelchair users, sweeping robots, humanoid robots, and quadrupedal robots. We use real-world 3D scans <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>, <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite> and annotate navigation graphs  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>, <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>, <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite> to allow plural solutions and per-edge traversability analysis. CapNav inputs the agent description, realistic indoor videos, key spatial reference nodes, and a navigation task as“from A to B”. We then examine VLM outputs for the prediction of feasibility, the navigation path, and reasoning validity. In total, CapNav contains 45 scenes, 2365 navigation tasks, and 5075 traversability annotations as ground truth.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Using the CapNav benchmark, we systematically study 13 opensource and proprietary VLMs under varying inference settings. Through quantitative and qualitative analysis, we diagnose three major observations: (1) <span id="S1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">mobility degradation</span>: navigation performance drops significantly when considering mobility capabilities; (2) <span id="S1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">visual bottleneck</span>: increasing visual input does not always lead to a performance boost in CapNav; (3) <span id="S1.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">spatial dimension blindness</span>: all models fail to detect non-traversability arising from insufficient spatial clearance (e.g., narrow passages or limited turning radius).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">These results highlight that substantial progress is still needed before VLM-based navigation can reliably support embodiment-specific deployment, particularly in safety-critical scenarios. Moreover, current VLM architectures and training paradigms remain limited in their ability to integrate spatial information across multiple visual frames and to perform precise metric reasoning in complex environments. Advancing embodied navigation, therefore, requires improvements in large-scale visual integration, geometry-grounded reasoning, and training objectives that explicitly encode mobility constraints and spatial dimension awareness.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Our contributions are threefold:</p>
<ol id="S1.I1" class="ltx_enumerate ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The CapNav benchmark.</span> We introduce <span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span>, a capability-conditioned VLN benchmark that evaluates how VLMs navigate complex indoor environments under realistic mobility constraints across five representative human and robot embodiments.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comprehensive evaluation of VLMs.</span> We conduct a head-to-head assessment of 13 state-of-the-art VLMs on capability-aware feasibility prediction, path validity, route traversability, and reasoning quality.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Guidelines and resources.</span> We analyze the effects of input frame rates, model settings, obstacle types, and failure modes, providing actionable guidelines for capability-aware navigation. We release the full dataset—videos, tasks, agent profiles, and 5k+ traversability annotations—along with an interactive annotation interface for extending CapNav to new agents and environments.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>Vision Language Navigation and Benchmarks</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) studies how an agent follows natural-language instructions using grounded visual observations to traverse an environment and reach a goal <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">67</a>]</cite>. Since the introduction of Room-to-Room (R2R) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>, which casts indoor navigation as step-by-step action selection on a sparse connectivity graph, a wide range of datasets and benchmarks have expanded VLN along multiple axes. Indoor instruction-following has been scaled in path length, diversity, and grounding density (e.g., R4R <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite> and RxR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite>); broader urban/street settings have also been explored (e.g., TOUCHDOWN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, StreetLearn <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite>, CityLearn <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>, CityWalker <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite>, Talk2Nav <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">53</a>]</cite>). Other benchmarks couple navigation with object grounding or task execution (e.g., REVERIE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite>, ALFRED <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">48</a>]</cite>, ObjectNav <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>, EmbodiedBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib65" title="" class="ltx_ref">64</a>]</cite>), while newer efforts probe long-horizon and open-ended embodied behaviors (e.g., GOAT-bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite> and NavBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib64" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>]</cite>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond task variants, VLN benchmarks differ in their observation and interaction assumptions. The canonical setting is <em id="S2.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">interactive</em>: an agent explores incrementally, receiving egocentric observations and accumulating spatial knowledge step-by-step. In contrast, a <em id="S2.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">passive</em> formulation provides global context, such as panoramic scans or pre-recorded videos, aiming to evaluate high-level spatial reasoning while reducing confounds from exploration and low-level control. For example, VideoNavQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite> replaces interactive navigation with oracle trajectory videos to isolate embodied visual reasoning; NRNS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib66" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite> learns image-goal navigation from passive roaming videos without online RL or a simulator; and PONI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib67" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite> trains an object-search module interaction-free from offline semantic maps. OpenEQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite> further supports an episodic-memory (video) setting that evaluates spatial memory and reasoning over recorded tours and scans. Under such passive formulations, the task increasingly resembles route planning and feasibility assessment; following prior work <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>, we still refer to this setting as navigation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Our goal—benchmarking VLM navigation validity under explicit mobility constraints—benefits from global observation, since it allows models to reason about traversability and alternative routes across the entire scene while isolating embodiment constraints from exploration and execution noise. We further adopt a graph-based spatial abstraction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>, <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite> to support pluralistic solutions and enable fine-grained evaluation of path feasibility and validity. This complements existing VLN benchmarks by enabling structured, capability-conditioned comparisons across real-world environments and embodiments.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Navigation with mobility constraints</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Past navigation research has modeled a wide range of mobility constraints, including accessibility for wheelchair users <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>, <a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, <a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">65</a>]</cite>, assistance for people who are blind or low vision <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">55</a>, <a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>, <a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>, and robotics embodiments such as quadrupeds <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>, <a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>, <a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite>, humanoids <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>, and vehicles operating over varied terrain <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>, <a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>. Some works also consider settings where multiple mobility profiles co-exist, either through simulator diversity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib59" title="" class="ltx_ref">58</a>, <a href="#bib.bib60" title="" class="ltx_ref">59</a>, <a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">60</a>]</cite> or by modeling user preferences <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite>. Collectively, these studies highlight that embodiment constraints materially change feasible routes and navigation strategies.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">However, most evaluations remain siloed—focusing on a single embodiment, environment family, or constraint type—making cross-embodiment comparison difficult on matched tasks. Recent efforts begin to address this gap: VLN-PE (introduced with a holistic study of physical and visual disparities) enables systematic cross-embodiment evaluation in a physically grounded simulator setting <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib62" title="" class="ltx_ref">54</a>]</cite>; NaviTrace <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">56</a>]</cite> evaluates embodiment-conditioned navigation via 2D trace prediction in real-world images; and VAMOS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite> introduces an affordance-grounded hierarchical planner to modulate plans by embodiment capabilities. Nonetheless, existing benchmarks either emphasize simulator-centric embodiment effects or cast the problem as trace/plan prediction without explicitly validating pluralistic, capability-conditioned route feasibility in complex indoor spaces with realistic navigation obstacles (e.g., multi-floor transitions, bottlenecks, and accessibility-specific affordances).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>The CapNav Benchmark</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce <em id="S3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Capability-conditioned Navigation</em> (CapNav), a benchmark for assessing how well can VLMs navigate in built environments given particular physical capabilities.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Problem Statement</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the CapNav task, each query instance is defined by a <em id="S3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Space–Task–Capability</em> triple</p>
<table id="S3.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle\mathcal{S},\tau,\mathbf{a}\rangle," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐚</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle\mathcal{S},\tau,\mathbf{a}\rangle,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the space <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> is represented by a touring video and a set of key spatial nodes; <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is a natural-language navigation goal specifying the source and target locations; and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐚</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}</annotation></semantics></math> is an agent profile encoding physical dimensions and operational abilities.
Given <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle\mathcal{S},\tau,\mathbf{a}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐚</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle\mathcal{S},\tau,\mathbf{a}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, a vision language model produces</p>
<table id="S3.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\hat{y},\hat{P},\hat{\rho})\;=\;f_{\theta}(\mathcal{S},\tau,\mathbf{a})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\hat{y},\hat{P},\hat{\rho})\;=\;f_{\theta}(\mathcal{S},\tau,\mathbf{a}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}\!\in\!\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em">∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}\!\in\!\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes task feasibility (<span id="S3.SS1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">can</span> / <span id="S3.SS1.p1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">cannot</span> complete), <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}=[v_{0},\dots,v_{m}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}=[v_{0},\dots,v_{m}]</annotation></semantics></math> is a node sequence representing the proposed navigation path, and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\rho}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\rho}</annotation></semantics></math> is a concise rationale explaining infeasibility when <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}\!=\!0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.108em">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}\!=\!0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This formulation enables CapNav to holistically evaluate a VLM’s capability-aware navigation ability. We assess performance from four complementary aspects: (i) <em id="S3.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">navigation feasibility</em>, (ii) <em id="S3.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">path validity</em>, (iii) <em id="S3.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">traversability accuracy</em>, and (iv) <em id="S3.SS1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">reasoning quality</em> for infeasible cases.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18424v1/data_annotation.png" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:685/128;" width="685" height="128" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S3.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Overview of CapNav’s data construction: Starting from a 3D indoor scan, we manually record a touring video and a navigation graph. We then use Gemini to generate natural language navigation tasks. Finally, per-task and per-agent traversability are annotated by manually controlling agents in the annotation interface.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Space.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each space <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> is a scanned 3D indoor environment comprising multiple interconnected rooms. As discussed in <a href="#S2.SS1" title="2.1 Vision Language Navigation and Benchmarks ‣ 2 Related Work ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">subsection 2.1</span></a>, we provide spatial information as a rendered touring video <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}=\{x_{t}\}_{t=1}^{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}=\{x_{t}\}_{t=1}^{T}</annotation></semantics></math>. To better ground the navigation to language description, we manually create a connectivity graph <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}=(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}=(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E})</annotation></semantics></math> over semantically meaningful spatial nodes (e.g., <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">kitchen</span>, <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">entry foyer</span>, <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">hallway</span>) and edges that denote directly walkable connections between the nodes. At inference, we only provide the video and the node list.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Task.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A navigation task <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is a natural-language instruction specifying a movement goal from a source node to a target node (<span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.,</span> “<em id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">From the wooden cabinet in the entrance foyer, go to the desk area in the master bedroom.</em>”).
Formally, each goal <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> can be expressed as a directed pair:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau:(v_{\mathrm{src}},d_{\mathrm{src}})\;\rightarrow\;(v_{\mathrm{tgt}},d_{\mathrm{tgt}}),\quad v_{\mathrm{src}},v_{\mathrm{tgt}}\in\mathcal{V}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>src</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>src</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>tgt</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>tgt</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>src</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>tgt</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau:(v_{\mathrm{src}},d_{\mathrm{src}})\;\rightarrow\;(v_{\mathrm{tgt}},d_{\mathrm{tgt}}),\quad v_{\mathrm{src}},v_{\mathrm{tgt}}\in\mathcal{V},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\mathrm{src}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>src</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\mathrm{src}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\mathrm{tgt}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>tgt</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\mathrm{tgt}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the source and target nodes in <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{src}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>src</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{src}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{tgt}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>tgt</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{tgt}}</annotation></semantics></math> are their corresponding natural-language descriptions specifying the precise starting and ending positions within those nodes (<span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.,</span> “<em id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">at the wooden cabinet in the entrance foyer</em>”, “<em id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">beside the desk area in the master bedroom</em>”).
This representation captures both the high-level spatial nodes and the finer-grained textual localization needed for realistic indoor navigation reasoning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Agent Profiles</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We specify the mobility capabilities <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐚</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}</annotation></semantics></math> with five distinct but representative agent profiles that cover human mobility and common robot platforms. <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Adult with no motor disabilities</span> represent a default condition where all indoor routes can be achieved; <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Wheelchair users</span> cannot use stairs and require clearance for passing and turning; <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Humanoid robot</span> cannot go up/down stairs and require clearance for passing; <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Sweeping robots</span> require a flat floor surface; <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Quadrupedal robots</span> can traverse most indoor spaces but cannot operate doors/elevators.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Each profile is described by a capability json
<math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}=(\phi,\kappa,\mu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐚</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}=(\phi,\kappa,\mu)</annotation></semantics></math>,
where <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> captures the physical footprint; <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> captures vertical traversal limits, including vertical height of a single obstacle, and whether the agent can cross continuous stairs; and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>μ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu</annotation></semantics></math> captures operation/manipulation abilities. These attributes directly affect traversability on edges <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}</annotation></semantics></math> and on overall tasks <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. See <a href="#S3.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Agent Profiles ‣ 3.1 Problem Statement ‣ 3 The CapNav Benchmark ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 4</span></a> for examples.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18424v1/agent.png" id="S3.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:685/530;" width="685" height="530" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S3.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Examples of CapNav’s agent profiles. Left: each profile specifies the physical dimensions and functional capabilities. Right: the agents’ physical dimensions are rendered and maneuvered in the 3D scenes to help confirm traversability.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Ground Truth of Traversability</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Traversability is manually annotated per-task and per-agent type. They are binary labels at the <em id="S3.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">edge</em> level, allowing multiple possible routes and providing more precise reasoning if a route is not traversable. For each navigation task <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> and embodiment <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐚</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}</annotation></semantics></math>, annotators iterate through each possible simple path that connects <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\mathrm{src}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>src</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\mathrm{src}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\mathrm{tgt}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>tgt</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\mathrm{tgt}}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>, and assign
<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{e}^{(\mathbf{a})}\in\{0,1\}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{e}^{(\mathbf{a})}\in\{0,1\},</annotation></semantics></math> to each edge <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> on these paths,
indicating whether <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> is passable under <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐚</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}</annotation></semantics></math> given local spatial geometry and mobility capabilities. Reasons for non-traversability are annotated as text descriptions (<span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.,</span> “<em id="S3.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">cannot go up/down stairs</em>”). The annotation UI visualizes 3D colliders matching <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> and supports manually controlled moving/turning to verify clearance and turning space (Fig. <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.1 Problem Statement ‣ 3 The CapNav Benchmark ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Given per-edge labels, we can then define the feasibility ground truth for a task <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s,g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s,g)</annotation></semantics></math> as the existence of at least one simple path (an acyclic sequence of distinct nodes) <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(v_{\mathrm{src}},v_{\mathrm{tgt}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>src</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>tgt</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(v_{\mathrm{src}},v_{\mathrm{tgt}})</annotation></semantics></math> that connects <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\mathrm{src}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>src</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\mathrm{src}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\mathrm{tgt}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>tgt</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\mathrm{tgt}}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>, where all edges are traversable:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="y^{\star}=\mathbb{I}\!\big[\exists\,P(v_{\mathrm{src}},v_{\mathrm{tgt}})\!:\!\forall(u,v)\!\in\!P,\,g^{(\mathbf{a})}_{(u,v)}=1\big]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mpadded style="width:0.219em;" width="0.219em"><mi>𝕀</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mo rspace="0.337em">∃</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>src</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>tgt</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.108em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.108em">:</mo><mo>∀</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em">∈</mo><mi>P</mi><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{\star}=\mathbb{I}\!\big[\exists\,P(v_{\mathrm{src}},v_{\mathrm{tgt}})\!:\!\forall(u,v)\!\in\!P,\,g^{(\mathbf{a})}_{(u,v)}=1\big],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Dataset</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We collect 3D indoor scenes from HM3D <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite> and Matterport3D <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>, and record touring videos in the Habitat simulator <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite> by manually navigating each space. Videos are rendered at 2FPS from human-eye height (<math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.5m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.5</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.5m</annotation></semantics></math>) with a <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75\textdegree" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>75</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>°</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75\textdegree</annotation></semantics></math> field of view to mimic casual handheld walkthroughs. For each scene, we construct a navigation graph via a custom annotation interface: nodes <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v\!\in\!\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em">∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v\!\in\!\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math> are annotated with semantic labels <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c(v)</annotation></semantics></math> and approximate 3D positions, and edges <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e=(u,v)\!\in\!\mathcal{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em">∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e=(u,v)\!\in\!\mathcal{E}</annotation></semantics></math> denote bidirectional, directly walkable connections. We provide each scene’s video and node list to Gemini 2.5 Pro to generate navigation tasks, manually verify task validity, and annotate edge-level traversability for five embodiments, including reasons for non-traversable cases. After filtering out scenes with major holes, disconnected subspaces, repetitive semantics, or trivial layouts, we retain 45 indoor scenes (avg. 160.38 s per video, 13.8 nodes, 14.5 edges), yielding 2,365 navigation tasks and 5,075 traversability labels (3,945 positive, 1,130 negative). Feasibility varies substantially across agent types in both task-level and edge-level ratios (see <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3.3 Dataset ‣ 3 The CapNav Benchmark ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table 1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S3.T1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 1</span>: </span><span id="S3.T1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Ratio of feasible task and traversable edges per agent type</span></figcaption>

<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Metrics &amp; Scoring</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate model outputs against ground truth using four complementary metrics, reported both overall and per-embodiment. Let
<math id="S3.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}=(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}=(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E})</annotation></semantics></math> be the space graph, let
<math id="S3.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(v_{\mathrm{src}},v_{\mathrm{tgt}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>src</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>tgt</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(v_{\mathrm{src}},v_{\mathrm{tgt}})</annotation></semantics></math> denote a simple path in <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>, and let
<math id="S3.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E(\hat{P})\subseteq\mathcal{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊆</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E(\hat{P})\subseteq\mathcal{E}</annotation></semantics></math> be the ordered edge set of a predicted path <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">(1) Feasibility Classification (<span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Feas-F1</span>).</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> be the model’s feasibility prediction and <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> the ground truth (Sec. <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Ground Truth of Traversability ‣ 3 The CapNav Benchmark ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>). We report positive-class precision, recall, and <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">(2) Path Validity (<span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">PV</span>).</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A predicted route <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}=[v_{0},\ldots,v_{m}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}=[v_{0},\ldots,v_{m}]</annotation></semantics></math> is considered valid if
(i) <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{i}\!\in\!\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em">∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{i}\!\in\!\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>,
(ii) <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(v_{i},v_{i+1})\!\in\!\mathcal{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em">∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(v_{i},v_{i+1})\!\in\!\mathcal{E}</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>,
(iii) <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{0}\!=\!v_{\mathrm{src}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em">=</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>src</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{0}\!=\!v_{\mathrm{src}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{m}\!=\!v_{\mathrm{tgt}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em">=</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>tgt</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{m}\!=\!v_{\mathrm{tgt}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and
(iv) <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}</annotation></semantics></math> is a simple path (no node repetitions).
We report:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{PV}=\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{I}(\hat{P}\in\mathcal{P}_{\text{simple}}(v_{\mathrm{src}},v_{\mathrm{tgt}}))\big]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>PV</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mi>𝕀</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mtext>simple</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>src</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>tgt</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{PV}=\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{I}(\hat{P}\in\mathcal{P}_{\text{simple}}(v_{\mathrm{src}},v_{\mathrm{tgt}}))\big].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">(3) Route Traversability Accuracy (<span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RTA</span>).</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Conditioned on <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}=1</annotation></semantics></math> and a valid <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}</annotation></semantics></math>, we evaluate the fraction of edges in <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}</annotation></semantics></math> that are actually traversable under embodiment <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐚</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{RTA}(\hat{P},\mathbf{a})\;=\;\frac{\sum_{e\in E(\hat{P})}g_{e}^{(\mathbf{a})}}{|E(\hat{P})|}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>RTA</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{RTA}(\hat{P},\mathbf{a})\;=\;\frac{\sum_{e\in E(\hat{P})}g_{e}^{(\mathbf{a})}}{|E(\hat{P})|},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{e}^{(\mathbf{a})}\!\in\!\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em">∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{e}^{(\mathbf{a})}\!\in\!\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> is the edge-level traversability label.
All edges are assigned unit weight so each edge contributes equally.
<math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{RTA}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>RTA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{RTA}=1</annotation></semantics></math> indicates a fully valid route, while lower values quantify partial failures.
This metric serves a role analogous to path-quality measures such as SPL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>, but conditions on embodiment-specific traversability.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">(4) Reasoning Validity (<span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RV</span>).</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For infeasible predictions (<math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}=0</annotation></semantics></math>), the model must (i) return a proposed route <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}</annotation></semantics></math> and (ii) provide a short rationale <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\rho}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\rho}</annotation></semantics></math> explaining the failure. Let <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}^{\star}(\hat{P},\mathbf{a})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}^{\star}(\hat{P},\mathbf{a})</annotation></semantics></math> be the set of annotated failure reasons, we define an LLM-as-judge function <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\text{LLM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>J</mi><mtext>LLM</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\text{LLM}}</annotation></semantics></math> that returns <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> if the model’s rationale semantically matches the annotation and <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> otherwise. We also verified the reliability of this function by manually validating 300 randomly sampled VLM reasonings. The results show an 89% alignment between human and LLM verdicts, indicating the precision and effectiveness of the LLM-as-judge method. We report RV as the mean of binary judgments:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{RV}\;=\;\mathbb{E}\!\left[J_{\text{LLM}}\!\big(\hat{\rho},\mathcal{R}^{\star}(\hat{P},\mathbf{a})\big)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>RV</mi><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mtext>LLM</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{RV}\;=\;\mathbb{E}\!\left[J_{\text{LLM}}\!\big(\hat{\rho},\mathcal{R}^{\star}(\hat{P},\mathbf{a})\big)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Composite CapNav Score.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report a composite score that aggregates the above aspects:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{CapNav}\;=\;\lambda_{c}\,F_{1}\;+\;\lambda_{p}\,\mathrm{PV}\;+\;\lambda_{t}\,\overline{\mathrm{RTA}}\;+\;\lambda_{r}\,\overline{\mathrm{RV}},\sum\lambda_{\cdot}=1," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>CapNav</mi><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>PV</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.502em" rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>RTA</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>RV</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mo>⋅</mo></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{CapNav}\;=\;\lambda_{c}\,F_{1}\;+\;\lambda_{p}\,\mathrm{PV}\;+\;\lambda_{t}\,\overline{\mathrm{RTA}}\;+\;\lambda_{r}\,\overline{\mathrm{RV}},\sum\lambda_{\cdot}=1,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\mathrm{RTA}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>RTA</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\mathrm{RTA}}</annotation></semantics></math> averages over positive predictions, and <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\mathrm{RV}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>RV</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\mathrm{RV}}</annotation></semantics></math> averages over negative predictions. We report per-embodiment scores and a macro-average across embodiments. By default, we set all <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> as 0.25.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reference Upper and Lower Bounds.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To contextualize model performance, we establish both lower and upper reference bounds under the proposed evaluation metrics. As a lower bound, we simulate a random-walk policy on the navigation graph that ignores scene structure and agent capability constraints. This naive baseline achieves a CapNav score of 0.29. As an approximate upper bound, we evaluate human performance on the same task. We recruited four human participants, each completing 20 randomly sampled navigation tasks using the same input and output format as the models. Human CapNav scores range from 0.49 to 0.75 (<span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">AVG</span> = 0.61).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T2" class="ltx_table">
<div id="S3.T2.3" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:710.4pt;height:203.2pt;vertical-align:-99.6pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-88.8pt,25.4pt) scale(0.8,0.8) ;">
<table id="S3.T2.3.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S3.T2.3.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S3.T2.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"><span id="S3.T2.3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Model</span></th>
<td id="S3.T2.3.1.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="S3.T2.3.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Feas-F1</span></td>
<td id="S3.T2.3.1.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="S3.T2.3.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">PV</span></td>
<td id="S3.T2.3.1.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="S3.T2.3.1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RTA</span></td>
<td id="S3.T2.3.1.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="S3.T2.3.1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RV</span></td>
<td id="S3.T2.3.1.1.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt"><span id="S3.T2.3.1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">CapNav</span></td>

</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S3.T2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 2</span>: </span><span id="S3.T2.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
CapNav performance across 13 VLMs. Each number indicate the best performance under all tested frame settings.
Left block reports each task metrics (Feas-F1, PV, RTA, RV, CapNav).
Right block reports per-agent composite scores for the five agent types: adult with no motor disabilities, humanoid robot, quadrupedal, sweeping robots, and wheelchair users.
Bold number indicate best per block. Blue indicate open-sourced model; Green indicate proprietary; Orange indicate spatial reasoning models.
