</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiments</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our experiments address three research questions:</p>
<ol id="S4.I1" class="ltx_enumerate ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RQ1:</span> How do state-of-the-art VLMs perform on <span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span>?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RQ2:</span> How does performance vary across models, agent types, and inference settings?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RQ3:</span> What failure modes expose the current limitations of these models?</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="S4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">To answer these questions, we evaluate 13 modern VLMs on <span id="S4.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span>. We report quantitative results stratified by model family, agent type, inference setting (frame budget and thinking mode), and challenge type. We further analyze common failure cases and consolidate them into a qualitative error taxonomy.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Settings</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluated 13 VLMs in November 2025, spanning popular proprietary and open-source models with strong multimodal capabilities, including the Gemini 2.5 family, GPT 4.1 and 5-Pro, Doubao-Seed, and Qwen3-VL. For models that expose a thinking option, we report results under both <em id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">thinking</em> and <em id="S4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">non-thinking</em> configurations. We additionally include Spatial-MLLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">57</a>]</cite> and Video-R1 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>, which explicitly target spatial reasoning—a core requirement of <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span>. Proprietary models are accessed via APIs, while open-source models are deployed on either a single NVIDIA A100 GPU (80GB) or a single A40 GPU (48GB).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At inference time, each model receives <span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span> tasks as a triple <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle\mathcal{S},\tau,\mathbf{a}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐚</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle\mathcal{S},\tau,\mathbf{a}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> (Section <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Problem Statement ‣ 3 The CapNav Benchmark ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>). Depending on model I/O constraints, <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> is provided either as a video clip or as a set of uniformly sampled frames. A practical limitation of current VLM interfaces is the maximum number of visual tokens/frames accepted per request. To study this constraint, we evaluate up to four input settings for each model (subject to interface limits): <span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">16</span>, <span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">32</span>, and <span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">64</span> total frames per clip, and a <span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1 FPS</span> setting that samples the full video (avg. 163 frames/video).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Performance</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Using the metrics in Section <a href="#S3.SS4" title="3.4 Metrics &amp; Scoring ‣ 3 The CapNav Benchmark ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a>, we compare model outputs against the ground-truth navigation graph to compute overall and per-agent performance. Table <a href="#S3.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Reference Upper and Lower Bounds. ‣ 3.4 Metrics &amp; Scoring ‣ 3 The CapNav Benchmark ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> summarizes performance metrics across all models under both <em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">thinking</em> and <em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">non-thinking</em> settings. We show the best metrics when multiple input frame settings are tested.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">All evaluated models outperform the random-walk baseline (CapNav = 29.35%). The strongest performance is achieved by proprietary models (notably the Gemini-2.5 family and GPT-5-pro), which exceed the human average (CapNav = 60.59%) but remain below the best human performance (CapNav = 74.77%). Overall, results show a clear separation between top-tier closed-source systems and the remainder of the field.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Models explicitly designed for spatial reasoning (Spatial-MLLM and Video-R1-7B) perform substantially worse across all metrics, despite claims of strong spatial performance. This indicates that their spatial reasoning training schemes and architectural modifications are not yet sufficient to address the challenges posed by <span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We also test the sensitivity of rankings to the CapNav score composition. In addition to equal weighting, we evaluate four alternative schemes that assign weight <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> to one component and <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/6</annotation></semantics></math> to each of the remaining components. Kendall’s <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> between rankings across these schemes averages <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.909" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.909</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.909</annotation></semantics></math>, suggesting that conclusions are largely robust to moderate weight changes.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Failure-mode taxonomy</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To characterize systematic errors, we use Gemini-3 to mine recurring error themes from 1,000 randomly sampled inference outputs, and then manually refine these themes into a four-category taxonomy. We then visualize the VLM predicted results of 1500 QA pairs sampled under 10 model settings in 3D scenes to measure the prevalence and distribution of each error type.</p>
<ul id="S4.I2" class="ltx_itemize ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S4.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Path hallucination:</span> (N = 659 / 1500) the predicted path links non-adjacent nodes, or violates the specified start/end, indicating an incorrect reasoning of the scene connectivity.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Obstacle hallucination:</span> (N = 418) the model reports non-existent blocking obstacles (e.g., “closed doors” or severe clutter), suggesting unreliable spatial interpretation of visual evidence.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dimension neglect:</span> (N = 191) the model overlooks geometric constraints that block the agent (e.g., narrow doors, tight clearances, cluttered passages), reflecting weak grounding between spatial extent and traversability.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Ability hallucination:</span> (N = 10) the output reasoning contradicts the provided agent profile. This failure is only observed in smaller open-sourced models (e.g., MiMo-VL 7B).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Physical Obstacle Types</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We further stratify by major obstacle categories in the traversability ground truth. We observe four major types of ground-truth obstacles: <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">stairs</span> (N = 520 / 2365), which block humanoid robots, sweeping robots, and wheelchair users; <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">door sill/floor height differences</span> (N = 82), which stop wheelchair users and sweeping robots; <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">narrow pathways</span> (N = 438), usually caused by narrow doors or furniture clutter, which can restrict humanoid robots, and also wheelchair users in extreme cases; <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">lacking of turning spaces</span> (N = 28), which hinders wheelchair users and, in rare cases, quadrupedal robots. For the navigation tasks labeled as non-traversable due to one or more of these obstacles, we evaluate how often VLMs can both correctly predict infeasibility and provide appropriate reasoning. The results are visualized in <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4.4 Physical Obstacle Types ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18424v1/figure/obstacle_performance.png" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:514/617;" width="514" height="617" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F5.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S4.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Model accuracy by obstacle type.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Findings</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Drawing on both quantitative results and qualitative inspection of model outputs, we distill three primary findings. Collectively, they indicate that current VLM-based navigation remains brittle under capability constraints, visually demanding inputs, and geometry-sensitive traversability judgments. We also summarize actionable guidance for practitioners and outline concrete directions for future work.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Capability constraints induce systematic performance degradation</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Across all tested models, performance is highest under the baseline embodiment without mobility limitations (adults without mobility constraints; mean <span id="S5.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span> score <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=57.83\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>57.83</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=57.83\%</annotation></semantics></math>). As constraints tighten, performance degrades. The largest gap appears for the <span id="S5.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HUMANOID</span> embodiment, which diverges most from the <span id="S5.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HUMAN</span> setting due to (i) an inability to climb stairs and (ii) a minimum pathway clearance requirement of <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.9\,\mathrm{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.9</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.9\,\mathrm{m}</annotation></semantics></math>; this configuration attains the lowest average score (mean <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=39.12\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>39.12</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=39.12\%</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This pattern highlights systematic deficits and imbalances in VLM-based navigation under mobility constraints. Strong performance in human-like settings does not translate to capability-constrained scenarios; hence, targeted evaluation is essential before VLM deployment in safety-critical navigation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The five agent types supported in <span id="S5.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span> are chosen to represent common human and robotic mobility profiles. As such, our results generalize to a wide range of practical embodiments. Practitioners may approximate expected model performance for their own systems by aligning their agent’s capabilities with the closest of the five provided profiles. For embodiments that differ substantially, <span id="S5.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span>’s open-sourced annotation interface and data curation pipeline allow users to define new agent profiles and extend the benchmark. This facilitates capability-aware evaluation for diverse hardware platforms and emerging robotic systems.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Increasing visual budget helps, but exposes a visual bottleneck</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Comparing matched inference settings with and without <em id="S5.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">thinking</em>, we find consistent improvements when <em id="S5.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">thinking</em> is enabled. Across 9 matched pairs, <em id="S5.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">thinking</em> configurations outperform their non-<em id="S5.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">thinking</em> counterparts by an average of <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.SS2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span> <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=6.87\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>6.87</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=6.87\%</annotation></semantics></math>. This gain is accompanied by a substantial compute cost: in our measurements, mean inference time increases by approximately <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="8\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8\times</annotation></semantics></math> (from <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14.94\,\mathrm{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>14.94</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14.94\,\mathrm{s}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="123.94\,\mathrm{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>123.94</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">123.94\,\mathrm{s}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Across the <span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">16</span>/<span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">32</span>/<span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">64</span>/<span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1 FPS</span> frame settings, latency is comparatively stable, but higher frame counts increase GPU VRAM and API costs. Performance generally improves with more frames; however, the marginal benefit is uneven, tending to be larger for stronger models (notably Gemini) and smaller or negligible for weaker models (see <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.2 Increasing visual budget helps, but exposes a visual bottleneck ‣ 5 Findings ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 6</span></a>). This pattern reveals a <em id="S5.SS2.p2.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">visual bottleneck</em>: additional evidence only helps if the model can reliably integrate it.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Qualitative inspection suggests two explanations:
(i) For most open-sourced models, 64 frames is already a very heavy input but it can still remain sparse in large or complex scenes, requiring robust cross-frame spatial integration and viewpoint alignment that weaker models often lack.
(ii) Additional viewpoints can increase <em id="S5.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">obstacle hallucinations</em> in some models: salient but non-blocking cues may be misinterpreted as traversal barriers, echoing prior observations about limitations in nonlocal reasoning for VLMs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">These results imply a cost–benefit frontier rather than a monotonic “more is better” rule. For <span id="S5.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span>-like VLN tasks, increasing inference budget can improve performance, but the return depends on model capacity and may trade off against latency, memory, cost, and even error modes.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18424v1/figure/frame_setting_performance_edited.png" id="S5.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:685/410;" width="685" height="410" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S5.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Performance across frame-budget settings. While higher frame counts can improve results, the gains are model-dependent and may saturate, consistent with a visual integration bottleneck.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Dimension neglect: models under-detect geometry-driven constraints</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">From our obstacle type analysis in <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4.4 Physical Obstacle Types ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 5</span></a>, all tested models perform markedly better on obstacles with salient visual signatures (e.g., stairs, door sills) than on constraints requiring implicit metric estimation (e.g., narrow clearances, turning radii). These failures indicate a recurring form of <em id="S5.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">dimension neglect</em>: traversability decisions that hinge on estimating size, clearance, or maneuvering space from images remain challenging for all tested VLMs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To probe whether the above deficits are learnable, we ran a pilot fine-tuning experiment. We augment the CapNav dataset on the navigation graph to expand the task count from 2K to 13K, and LoRA fine-tune on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct. After one epoch of training, test score improves from <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45.26\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>45.26</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45.26\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="55.18\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>55.18</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">55.18\%</annotation></semantics></math>, and the finetuned model generates more dimension-aware reasoning. However, reasoning validity decreases (<math id="S5.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.30\rightarrow 0.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.30</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.30\rightarrow 0.25</annotation></semantics></math>), and we observe frequent false positives on narrow passages (i.e., incorrectly flagging feasible routes as blocked).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">These outcomes suggest that fine-tuning can reduce dimension neglect but does not fully resolve geometric precision, and may shift the error profile toward overly aggressive obstacle judgments. This highlights the need to jointly optimize for <em id="S5.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">obstacle awareness</em> and <em id="S5.SS3.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">dimension reasoning</em>, rather than treating score improvements alone as sufficient.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Building on this pilot, we plan to explore RL-based tuning with task-level rewards under embodiment constraints. We also aim to experiment with spatial-information injection (depth estimates, topological priors, or map-like intermediate representations) to improve spatial dimension judgments.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We present <span id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span>, a benchmark that systematically evaluates capability-conditioned navigation across diverse embodiments, realistic mobility obstacles, and graph-structured indoor environments. By evaluating 13 state-of-the-art VLMs, we observe three consistent patterns. First, performance degrades systematically as mobility constraints tighten, indicating that strong results in unconstrained human-like settings do not transfer reliably to other embodiments. Second, increasing the inference budget (more frames or “thinking” mode) yields inconsistent gains and incurs computational cost, exposing a visual integration bottleneck. Third, models exhibit dimension neglect: they handle salient obstacles better but struggle with dimension reasoning (<span id="S6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.</span>, narrow clearances and turning radii). A pilot fine-tuning study suggests that these deficits are partially learnable, but fine-tuning may introduce false positives, highlighting the need to jointly optimize the spatial reasoning reliability in task formulation and spatial dimension. We release both the <span id="S6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CapNav</span> dataset and annotation tool.


<span id="S6.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text"></span></p>
</div>
</section>

<div id="p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="p4.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:144%;">Supplementary Material 
<br class="ltx_break"></span></p>
</div>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Overview of Supplementary Material</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This supplementary material provides examples of VLM input and output in the dataset generation and benchmark evaluation process. We include the following components:
(1) the exact prompts and input representations provided to VLMs,
(2) examples of ground truth</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">A. Task Generation</h2>

<section id="Sx2.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">A.1 Prompt Template</h3>

<div id="Sx2.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx2.SSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use a unified prompt template to instruct a VLM to
generate navigation tasks for each scene. The template
contains three components: (1) an overall instruction, (2) file attachments, <em id="Sx2.SSx1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">i.e</em>.<span id="Sx2.SSx1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text"></span> a scene video and a guideline document that contains more detailed instructions (Sec A.2-3), and
(3) a list of spatial nodes in the scene (Sec A.4).</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx2.SSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx2.SSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">An example of generated tasks can be found in <span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink ltx_path ltx_font_typewriter ltx_ref_self">taskGeneration/HM3D00025_tasks.json</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx2.SSx1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="401.39" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 687.5 401.39" width="687.5"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,401.39) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#CCCCCC;" fill="#CCCCCC" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 4.49 L 0 396.9 C 0 399.38 2.01 401.39 4.49 401.39 L 683.01 401.39 C 685.49 401.39 687.5 399.38 687.5 396.9 L 687.5 4.49 C 687.5 2.01 685.49 0 683.01 0 L 4.49 0 C 2.01 0 0 2.01 0 4.49 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FBFBFB;" fill="#FBFBFB" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.55 4.49 L 0.55 396.9 C 0.55 399.07 2.32 400.83 4.49 400.83 L 683.01 400.83 C 685.18 400.83 686.95 399.07 686.95 396.9 L 686.95 4.49 C 686.95 2.32 685.18 0.55 683.01 0.55 L 4.49 0.55 C 2.32 0.55 0.55 2.32 0.55 4.49 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 12.36 13.86)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:47.9em;--ltx-fo-height:27.26em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;" height="380.6" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 377.14)" width="662.8"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:47.9em;">
<span id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Instruction:
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:3.0pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
You are an expert benchmark question designer for the
Capability-Conditioned Navigation Benchmark.
You are provided with three materials:</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.I1" class="ltx_enumerate" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.2em;">
<span id="Sx2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<span id="Sx2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">A video showing the indoor environment.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="Sx2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<span id="Sx2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">A guideline PDF defining how to create navigation questions.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="Sx2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<span id="Sx2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">A list of valid scene nodes.</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1.1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Requirements:
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:3.0pt;">
Please strictly follow the guideline and generate realistic, visually
grounded, route-based navigation questions. Each question must:</span></span>
<span id="Sx2.I2" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.2em;">
<span id="Sx2.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="Sx2.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx2.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Include a start and end node with detailed in-room descriptions.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="Sx2.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="Sx2.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx2.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Follow the schema structure provided by the system.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="Sx2.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="Sx2.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx2.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Output a valid JSON array (no extra commentary).</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="Sx2.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="Sx2.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx2.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Ensure the total number of generated questions is </span><math id="Sx2.I2.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">≥</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq</annotation></semantics></math><span id="Sx2.I2.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> {min_questions}.</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1.1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">External files (video, pdf)<span id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1.1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Node List:
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:3.0pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx1.p3.pic1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
{node_list_text}</span></span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx2.SSx2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">A.2 Video Input</h3>

<div id="Sx2.SSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx2.SSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When generating navigation tasks, the VLM receives a touring video of the space.
In Fig.<a href="#Sx2.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ A.2 Video Input ‣ A. Task Generation ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, we show representative frames of an example video.
The full MP4 file is included in the supplementary ZIP, see <span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink ltx_path ltx_font_typewriter ltx_ref_self">taskGeneration/HM3D00025.mp4</span>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="Sx2.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18424v1/figure/HM3D25_frames.png" id="Sx2.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:685/120;" width="685" height="120" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="Sx2.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="Sx2.F7.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Representative frames from the input
video <span id="Sx2.F7.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">HM3D00025.mp4</span>. The VLM receives the complete MP4 video for navigation task generation.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="Sx2.SSx3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">A.3 Guideline Document</h3>

<div id="Sx2.SSx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx2.SSx3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide a carefully designed guideline document to the VLM to specify the exact type and format of the navigation tasks to be generated. We show an excerpt of the document below. The complete guideline is included in the supplementary ZIP
(<span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink ltx_path ltx_font_typewriter ltx_ref_self">taskGeneration/Generate_Tasks_Guidelines.pdf</span>).</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx2.SSx3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="255.18" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 687.5 255.18" width="687.5"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,255.18) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#CCCCCC;" fill="#CCCCCC" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.91 L 0 249.27 C 0 252.53 2.64 255.18 5.91 255.18 L 681.59 255.18 C 684.86 255.18 687.5 252.53 687.5 249.27 L 687.5 5.91 C 687.5 2.64 684.86 0 681.59 0 L 5.91 0 C 2.64 0 0 2.64 0 5.91 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FBFBFB;" fill="#FBFBFB" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.97 5.91 L 1.97 249.27 C 1.97 251.45 3.73 253.21 5.91 253.21 L 681.59 253.21 C 683.77 253.21 685.53 251.45 685.53 249.27 L 685.53 5.91 C 685.53 3.73 683.77 1.97 681.59 1.97 L 5.91 1.97 C 3.73 1.97 1.97 3.73 1.97 5.91 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 16.2)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.34em;--ltx-fo-height:16.28em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:10pt;" height="227.62" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 225.2)" width="696.56"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:50.34em;">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Guideline (excerpt):
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:-2.8pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Capability-conditioned navigability</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.3" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.4" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">1. Goal</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.5" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.5.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This guideline defines how to generate capability-neutral, route-based navigation questions for the Capability-Conditioned Navigation Benchmark. You are an AI model that generates route-based navigation questions from an indoor walkthrough video.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.6" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.6.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.6.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Your task is to create realistic and scene-consistent navigation tasks that test how [Agent] can move and act within the visible environment.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.7" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.7.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.8" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.8.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Each question must:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.9" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.9.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.9.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">1. Be fully grounded in the video (only describe objects, rooms, and connections that actually appear).</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.10" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.10.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">2. Use the provided list of scene nodes as the only valid room-level landmarks.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.11" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.11.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">...</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.12" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.12.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx2.SSx3.p2.pic1.1.12.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;"></span></span></span>

<section id="Sx2.SSx4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">A.4 Node List</h3>

<div id="Sx2.SSx4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx2.SSx4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To ground the sub-spaces in a scene, the VLM also receives a list of node IDs paired with textual descriptions. We instruct the VLM to reference these nodes when generating navigation tasks. Below we show a few nodes from the scene <span id="Sx2.SSx4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">HM3D00025</span>, taken directly from the scene
graph. The full JSON file is included in the supplementary ZIP
(<span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink ltx_path ltx_font_typewriter ltx_ref_self">groundTruth/HM3D00025-graph.json</span>).</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx2.SSx4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="Sx2.SSx4.p2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="221.28" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 687.5 221.28" width="687.5"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,221.28) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#CCCCCC;" fill="#CCCCCC" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.91 L 0 215.37 C 0 218.63 2.64 221.28 5.91 221.28 L 681.59 221.28 C 684.86 221.28 687.5 218.63 687.5 215.37 L 687.5 5.91 C 687.5 2.64 684.86 0 681.59 0 L 5.91 0 C 2.64 0 0 2.64 0 5.91 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FBFBFB;" fill="#FBFBFB" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.97 5.91 L 1.97 215.37 C 1.97 217.55 3.73 219.31 5.91 219.31 L 681.59 219.31 C 683.77 219.31 685.53 217.55 685.53 215.37 L 685.53 5.91 C 685.53 3.73 683.77 1.97 681.59 1.97 L 5.91 1.97 C 3.73 1.97 1.97 3.73 1.97 5.91 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 16.2)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:50.34em;--ltx-fo-height:13.83em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:10pt;" height="193.72" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 191.3)" width="696.56"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">

<section id="Sx3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">B. Benchmark Evaluation</h2>

<div id="Sx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When evaluating on the CapNav benchmark, we query VLMs to answer the
capability-conditioned navigation questions.
Each query provides the following inputs:</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="Sx3.I3" class="ltx_enumerate" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">
<li id="Sx3.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="Sx3.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx3.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">a specific indoor scene shown as a tour video (see <a href="#Sx2.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ A.2 Video Input ‣ A. Task Generation ‣ CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 7</span></a>),</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Sx3.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="Sx3.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx3.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">all nodes of the scene’s navigation graph,</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Sx3.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="Sx3.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx3.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">one navigation question,</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Sx3.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="Sx3.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx3.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">one agent profile describing the mobility capabilities.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="Sx3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The model must use both the video and the text inputs to determine whether the agent can complete the navigation task. Below we show a prompt example for scene <span id="Sx3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">HM3D00025</span> and agent <span id="Sx3.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Humanoid</span>. The original prompt file can also be seen in <span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink ltx_path ltx_font_typewriter ltx_ref_self">benchmarkEvaluation/HM3D00025_q01_HUMANOID.txt</span></p>
</div>
<section id="Sx3.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">B.1 Example Prompt (HM3D00025, HUMANOID)</h3>

<div id="Sx3.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="1890.02" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 687.5 1890.02" width="687.5"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,1890.02) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#CCCCCC;" fill="#CCCCCC" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 4.49 L 0 1885.53 C 0 1888.01 2.01 1890.02 4.49 1890.02 L 683.01 1890.02 C 685.49 1890.02 687.5 1888.01 687.5 1885.53 L 687.5 4.49 C 687.5 2.01 685.49 0 683.01 0 L 4.49 0 C 2.01 0 0 2.01 0 4.49 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FBFBFB;" fill="#FBFBFB" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.55 4.49 L 0.55 1885.53 C 0.55 1887.7 2.32 1889.46 4.49 1889.46 L 683.01 1889.46 C 685.18 1889.46 686.95 1887.7 686.95 1885.53 L 686.95 4.49 C 686.95 2.32 685.18 0.55 683.01 0.55 L 4.49 0.55 C 2.32 0.55 0.55 2.32 0.55 4.49 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 12.36 13.09)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:47.9em;--ltx-fo-height:134.9em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="1869.25" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 1866.56)" width="662.8"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:47.9em;">
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Instruction:
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:3.0pt;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
You are an expert visual reasoning agent for indoor navigation tasks. You will receive four materials:</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx3.I4" class="ltx_enumerate" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.2em;">
<span id="Sx3.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<span id="Sx3.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx3.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.I4.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">A video showing the indoor environment.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="Sx3.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<span id="Sx3.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx3.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.I4.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">A single navigation question asking whether the agent can move from one area (node) to another.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="Sx3.I4.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<span id="Sx3.I4.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx3.I4.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.I4.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The agent’s physical and capability profile.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="Sx3.I4.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<span id="Sx3.I4.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx3.I4.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.I4.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The list of all nodes in this environment, with their textual descriptions (e.g., room type, furniture, width of passages).</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Your goal is to determine whether the agent can successfully reach the destination area from the starting area,
based on both the video and the textual descriptions. You must reason step by step about spatial constraints,
obstacles, connectivity, and the agent’s mobility limitations.</span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Input:<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">

<br class="ltx_break"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1.Navigation Question:
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:3.0pt;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Can [Agent] move from the dark sectional sofa area in the main living space to the white L-shaped sofa area in the first floor living room?</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2.Agent Profile (HUMANOID):
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:-16.0pt;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:479.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:479.0pt;">
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Agent name: HUMANOID</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.7" class="ltx_p" style="width:479.0pt;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:479.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.7.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:479.0pt;">
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Body shape: box</span>
</span></span></span></span>

<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.21" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.21.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">4.Video<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.21.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">

<br class="ltx_break">(You can observe the video for spatial layout and obstacles.)</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.22" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.22.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Task:
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:3.0pt;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.22.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Your goal is to determine whether the agent can </span>navigate<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.22.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> from the start area to the goal area.

<br class="ltx_break">Focus exclusively on </span>movement feasibility<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.22.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">, considering physical dimensions, obstacle heights, and connection constraints.
<br class="ltx_break">You must </span>not stop after a single failed route attempt<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.22.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">. If one possible route is blocked (e.g., by stairs or narrow spaces),
you must </span>actively consider all other possible paths<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.22.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> between the start and goal nodes in the scene graph.
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:3.0pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.23" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.23.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Follow these principles:</span></span>
<span id="Sx3.I5" class="ltx_enumerate" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.2em;">
<span id="Sx3.I5.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<span id="Sx3.I5.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx3.I5.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.I5.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Explore </span><span id="Sx3.I5.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">all possible routes</span><span id="Sx3.I5.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> through the scene graph before deciding the task is impossible. That means, try </span><span id="Sx3.I5.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">multiple alternative routes</span><span id="Sx3.I5.i1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> using all visible connections in the scene graph until you are confident that </span><span id="Sx3.I5.i1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">no feasible route</span><span id="Sx3.I5.i1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> exists.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="Sx3.I5.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<span id="Sx3.I5.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx3.I5.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.I5.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Account for the agent’s capabilities (e.g., door opening, elevator operation, stair traversal) when evaluating possible paths.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="Sx3.I5.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<span id="Sx3.I5.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx3.I5.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.I5.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">When multiple feasible paths exist, select the </span><span id="Sx3.I5.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">most direct and realistic one</span><span id="Sx3.I5.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> given the agent’s capabilities.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="Sx3.I5.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<span id="Sx3.I5.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx3.I5.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.I5.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If no route works, specify which </span><span id="Sx3.I5.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">edge or physical barrier</span><span id="Sx3.I5.i4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> prevents traversal and explain why.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="Sx3.I5.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<span id="Sx3.I5.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="Sx3.I5.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.I5.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If a feasible route exists, specify the </span><span id="Sx3.I5.i5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">sequence of nodes</span><span id="Sx3.I5.i5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> representing the navigable path.</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.24" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.24.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Important: 
<br class="ltx_break">If you initially find the route impossible, <span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.24.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">re-examine the scene graph</span> and attempt at least two distinct alternative paths before concluding ”no”.
<br class="ltx_break">Your reasoning should reflect persistent exploration: do not assume failure after one obstacle; explore until all logical alternatives are ruled out.
<br class="ltx_break">You do not need to consider unrelated interactions (e.g., turning on lights, using computers, or touching furniture).</span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.25" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.25.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Please decide for each given question whether the agent can complete the navigation task. 
<br class="ltx_break">If yes, provide a <span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.25.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">feasible path</span> through the relevant nodes. 
<br class="ltx_break">If no, specify the <span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.25.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">edge (two connected nodes)</span> that blocks traversal and give a concise <span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.25.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">reason</span> (e.g., too narrow passage, stairs, or closed door). 
<br class="ltx_break">Your reasoning should always consider the agent’s physical capabilities mentioned in the Agent profile(e.g., wheelchair cannot climb stairs, sweeper robot cannot open doors).</span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.26" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.26.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Return your answer in the required structured JSON format below.</span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.27" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.27.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Output Format (JSON only):
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:-3.0pt;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.27.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.28" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.28.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:479.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.28.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:479.0pt;">
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.p15" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.p15.1" class="ltx_p">[</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.29" class="ltx_p" style="width:479.0pt;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.29.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:479.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.29.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:479.0pt;">
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.p16" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.p16.1" class="ltx_p">    ...</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.30" class="ltx_p" style="width:479.0pt;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.30.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:479.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.30.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:479.0pt;">
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.p17" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.p17.1" class="ltx_p">    {</span>

<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.31" class="ltx_p" style="width:479.0pt;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.31.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:479.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.31.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:479.0pt;">

<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.35" class="ltx_p" style="width:479.0pt;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.35.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:479.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.35.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:479.0pt;">

<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.36" class="ltx_p" style="width:479.0pt;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.36.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:479.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.36.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:479.0pt;">

</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.37" class="ltx_p" style="width:479.0pt;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.37.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:479.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx3.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.37.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:479.0pt;">

<section id="Sx4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">C. Reasoning Evaluation</h2>

<div id="Sx4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">CapNav deploys an LLM-as-judge method to evaluate whether a navigability explanation from a VLM’s output is consistent with the
ground-truth annotations. We provide the LLM judge with (1) the VLM-generated
reasoning for why a path is non-traversable and (2) the full ground-truth traversability record for the
path. The LLM will determine whether the explanation correctly
captures the underlying failure conditions.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Below we briefly present the prompts and data formats. For a full example, please check <span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink ltx_path ltx_font_typewriter ltx_ref_self">reasoningEvaluation/HM3D00025_q01_HUMANOID.txt</span></p>
</div>
<section id="Sx4.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">C.1 Prompt Template</h3>

<div id="Sx4.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="305.68" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 687.5 305.68" width="687.5"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,305.68) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#CCCCCC;" fill="#CCCCCC" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.91 L 0 299.78 C 0 303.04 2.64 305.68 5.91 305.68 L 681.59 305.68 C 684.86 305.68 687.5 303.04 687.5 299.78 L 687.5 5.91 C 687.5 2.64 684.86 0 681.59 0 L 5.91 0 C 2.64 0 0 2.64 0 5.91 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FBFBFB;" fill="#FBFBFB" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.97 5.91 L 1.97 299.78 C 1.97 301.95 3.73 303.71 5.91 303.71 L 681.59 303.71 C 683.77 303.71 685.53 301.95 685.53 299.78 L 685.53 5.91 C 685.53 3.73 683.77 1.97 681.59 1.97 L 5.91 1.97 C 3.73 1.97 1.97 3.73 1.97 5.91 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 16.89)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:49.27em;--ltx-fo-height:19.88em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.23em;font-size:10pt;" height="278.13" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 275.01)" width="681.76"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">

<span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Instruction (Reasoning Evaluation):<span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">

<span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.3" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;"></span></span></span>

</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.5" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">

<span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">1. A system-generated explanation of why a path is not traversable.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.6" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">

<span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Your task:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.9" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.9.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.9.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">

</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.10" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.10.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">

<span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.11" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.11.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">

</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.15" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.15.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx4.SSx1.p1.pic1.1.15.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">

<span id="Sx4.SSx2.p1.pic1.1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Sx4.SSx2.p1.pic1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx4.SSx2.p1.pic1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">
<span id="Sx4.SSx2.p1.pic1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx4.SSx2.p1.pic1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">System reasoning:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="Sx4.SSx2.p1.pic1.1.3" class="ltx_p" style="width:465.6pt;"><span id="Sx4.SSx2.p1.pic1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:465.6pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="Sx4.SSx2.p1.pic1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:465.6pt;">
<span id="Sx4.SSx2.p1.pic1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="Sx4.SSx2.p1.pic1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">"The agent cannot traverse stairs, and the only path between the</span>

    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
  </div>
